source: Sverige i fokus, chapter 11: Sverige och omvärlden (extra draft)
questionSv: Vilken påverkan har Sveriges medlemskap i EU på svensk lagstiftning?
questionEn: What effect does Sweden’s EU membership have on Swedish legislation?
options: Sverige måste följa EU:s gemensamma lagar, vilket påverkar en stor del av svensk lagstiftning.
EU har ingen påverkan på svensk lagstiftning, eftersom riksdagen beslutar helt oberoende i alla frågor.
Sveriges regering utses av EU-parlamentet i stället för av riksdagen.
Svenska domstolar får inte döma i brottmål utan godkännande från en EU-domstol.
optionsEn: Sweden must follow common EU laws, which affects a large part of Swedish legislation.
The EU has no effect on Swedish legislation, because the Riksdag decides completely independently in all matters.
Sweden’s government is appointed by the European Parliament instead of by the Riksdag.
Swedish courts may not judge criminal cases without approval from an EU court.
explanationEn: EU membership means Sweden must follow common EU laws, which significantly impact national legislation. The Riksdag does not act completely independently in areas where EU law applies.

questionSv: Vad ger svenska ambassader och konsulat dig som medborgare utomlands?
questionEn: What can Swedish embassies and consulates give you as a citizen abroad?
options: Hjälp vid nödsituationer, till exempel vid passförlust eller arrestering.
Rättslig immunitet så att du inte lyder värdlandets lag.
Ambassaden bokar och betalar alltid din hemresa vid reseproblem.
Du kan rösta i svenska val på ambassaden utan att vara folkbokförd.
optionsEn: Help in emergencies, for example if you lose your passport or are arrested.
Legal immunity so you do not obey the host country’s law.
The embassy always books and pays for your trip home when travel problems happen.
You can vote in Swedish elections at the embassy without being registered.
explanationEn: Consular help from Swedish embassies/consulates assists citizens abroad in emergencies (e.g., lost passport, arrest). It does not exempt you from local law, does not guarantee a free ticket home, and voting abroad requires being registered.
